name: tatter-foal

attributes.attribute: British bogle that shifts its shape
usually appears as a shaggy baby horse

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The tatter-foal was a British folk spirit. The name shag-foal was also used. The creature was a kind of bogle or bogey. It could take many shapes. It sometimes wore the shape of a monkey. Most often it appeared as a shaggy baby horse.

okr.objective: Record the tatter-foal as a shape-shifting British bogle.
key_results: Names the tatter-foal and its second name shag-foal
Notes it shifts into many forms, including a monkey
States its most common shape was a shaggy baby horse
